channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar holds steady as US Dollar retreats
item.description: NZD/USD trades around 0.5665 on Friday at the time of writing, virtually unchanged on the day, as the New Zealand Dollar (NZD) struggles to capitalize on a moderate decline in the US Dollar (USD).

item.title: Dow Jones Industrial Average bounces on Iran's latest Hormuz offer
item.description: Iran has offered to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days of Washington accepting its terms, and buyers have taken the Dow Jones Industrial Average higher before Washington has replied. The index trades near 51,800 on Friday and is on track to end a three-session losing run.

item.title: British Pound finds relief as USD pauses, but inflation risks linger
item.description: The Pound Sterling (GBP) trims some of its weekly losses, gaining over 0.18% against the US Dollar (USD) on Friday as the Greenback takes a breather, even as US Treasury yields continue to rise.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: Undervalued near 1.41 against US Dollar – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret note that the Canadian Dollar (CAD) is flat versus the US Dollar (USD) and lagging most G10 peers. They highlight that wider US–Canada yield spreads have weighed on the CAD, but see the move as stretched.

item.title: Gold struggles below $4,300, heads for weekly decline on hawkish Fed outlook
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) reverses earlier intraday gains on Friday, failing to capitalize on a modest pullback in the US Dollar as growing expectations that the Federal Reserve (Fed) may raise interest rates again weigh on the non-yielding metal.

item.title: Euro: Correction seen near key averages against US Dollar – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale’s Morning Briefing reports EUR/USD traded between 1.1359 and 1.1387 overnight and is on course for a second weekly drop. The defence of the 100‑week moving average at 1.1356 and oversold technicals suggest the correction may have run its course for now.

item.title: Euro set for third weekly decline as hawkish Federal Reserve outlook weighs
item.description: EUR/USD edges higher on Friday as the US Dollar (USD) pauses after a strong weekly rally, allowing the Euro (EUR) to recover some ground. However, the pair remains on track for a third consecutive weekly decline.

item.title: Australian Dollar: RBA hike expectations shape outlook – ING
item.description: ING economists Deepali Bhargava and Lynn Song expect the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) to raise rates by 25bp, citing a still-hot economy, tight labour market conditions and upside surprises in Gross Domestic Product (GDP) and inflation.

item.title: US Dollar: Yields support Greenback strength – OCBC
item.description: OCBC strategists Sim Moh Siong and Christopher Wong highlight that resilient US data, sticky inflation and elevated energy prices are pushing US Treasury yields higher and supporting the US Dollar.

item.title: Australian Dollar rebounds from 0.7000 as US Dollar eases after strong week
item.description: AUD/USD edges higher on Friday, trading around 0.7025 at the time of writing, up 0.20% on the day.

item.title: Mexican Peso: Banxico stance keeps bar high for hikes – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad reports that Banxico left its policy rate at 6.50% for a third consecutive meeting and removed prior guidance to keep it fixed, while stressing it does not need to match expected Federal Reserve hikes.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Pressure persists toward 159.60 against US Dollar - UOB
item.description: UOB’s Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann note USD/JPY has risen for five straight sessions to 158.83, with momentum still positive but indicators deeply overbought.

item.title: Euro: Credibility restored supports Dollar – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Thu Lan Nguyen notes that the Fed’s unanimous September rate hike has temporarily restored its credibility and supported the Dollar, prompting a lower EUR/USD year-end forecast to 1.15 from 1.17.

item.title: Canadian Dollar set for third weekly decline despite pullback in US Dollar
item.description: USD/CAD trades little changed on Friday as the US Dollar (USD) pulls back slightly after a strong rally this week. The pause in the Greenback and Treasury yields has offered little relief to the Canadian Dollar (CAD), leaving it on track for a third consecutive weekly decline.

item.title: Indian Rupee: RBI interventions cap losses against US Dollar – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale reports USD/INR has repeatedly tested 96.00 but failed to break higher as the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) maintained a visible presence in the FX market through interventions.

item.title: US Dollar: Back-end yields support USD consolidation – ING
item.description: ING strategists Francesco Pesole and Frantisek Taborsky note that rising back-end yields and risk-off sentiment are helping consolidate recent Dollar gains, even if they look stretched versus short-term fundamentals.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Range-bound against US Dollar as intervention risk looms – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad highlights that political comments from US and Japanese leaders helped push USD/JPY back below its 200-day moving average.

item.title: Australian Dollar: Weakness may extend toward 0.6970 against US Dollar - UOB
item.description: UOB’s Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann observe that AUD/USD extended its recent slide to 0.7006, with positive divergence hinting at slowing momentum but not yet a clear base.

item.title: Swedish Krona: Riksbank facing delayed inflation rebound – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Michael Pfister and Norman Liebke describe how Swedish government tax and fuel measures have temporarily suppressed inflation, keeping the Riksbank on hold at 1.75% with hikes only expected late in the year.

item.title: EUR/GBP Price Forecast: Bulls challenge 0.8600 resistance after weeks of consolidation
item.description: EUR/GBP trades flat around 0.8600 on Friday and is heading for a weekly gain as the Bank of England’s (BoE) wait-and-see stance weighs on the British Pound (GBP). The BoE has remained on hold so far this year, leaving its benchmark rate unchanged at 3.75% at last week’s meeting.

item.title: CEE FX: Regional currencies weaken against Euro on policy risks - Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale notes Central and Eastern European (CEE) currencies, including the Hungarian Forint (HUF), are set to weaken about 3% against the Euro (EUR) this week as EUR/USD falls below 1.14.

item.title: Japanese Yen extends recovery as Tokyo officials defend BoJ independence
item.description: The Japanese Yen pares losses against the US Dollar (USD) on Friday, as Japanese yields escalate, narrowing the gap with Treasury yields, while Japan’s Finance Minister (FM) Satsuki Katayama defended the independence of the Bank of Japan (BoJ).

item.title: Euro: France spreads weigh on EUR – ING
item.description: Francesco Pesole at ING sees EUR/USD downside risks persisting, with the 1.1320–1.1330 area as key support that could be tested quickly on stronger US data or another sharp Oil move higher.

item.title: US Dollar: Rate differentials support but upside constrained – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad notes that the recent pullback in Oil prices has eased global bond selling and cooled the Dollar rally.

item.title: Indian Rupee gets cushioned by RBI’s likely intervention on Friday
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) gains a temporary ground against the US Dollar (USD) on Friday after remaining under pressure in the past few days. The USD/INR pair struggles to extend gains above 95.96 on the likely Reserve Bank of India’s (RBI) intervention.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD reclaims $65 as rally in bond yields, US Dollar hits pause
item.description: Silver price (XAG/USD) is up 1.85% to near $65.00 during the European trading session on Friday. The white metal strengthens as rally in the US Dollar (USD) and United States (US) Treasury Yields appears to have hit a pause.

item.title: British Pound: Risk of test of 1.3140 against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: UOB’s Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann report that GBP/USD extended its sharp decline to 1.3205, leaving conditions deeply oversold but with the bias still pointing lower.

item.title: Fed’s Williams: Persistent supply shocks cannot be ignored
item.description: New York Federal Reserve (Fed) Bank John Willams said in a panel discussion at Oxford University on Friday that although tariffs and higher energy prices don’t to a sustainable inflation. However, repeated supply shocks are keeping price pressures higher.

item.title: WTI Oil reversal stalls above $91.00 as Middle East tensions outweigh supply increases
item.description: The price of the US benchmark West Texas Intermediate (WTI) barrel has stabilised above $91.00 on Friday, with the reversal from Thursday’s highs, near $96.00, losing momentum.

item.title: Japan’s Katayama: Takaichi very much respects the independence of the BoJ
item.description: Japanese Finance Minister (FM) Satsuki Katayama stresses on Bank of Japan’s (BoJ) independence while speaking during the European trading session on Friday. This is the second time in the day when Katayama has delivered remarks on economy and currency.
